name: Architecture-Grounded Governed Objective Lifecycle Composition
objective: Compose the graduated River Development Agent UNDERSTAND, PLAN, and GENERATE capabilities with the existing authoritative governed downstream lifecycle so a bounded repository objective can progress through architecture-grounded understanding, deterministic planning, governed implementation-intent generation, proposal and manifest derivation, artifact generation, governed execution-package creation and persistence, separately authorized execution, verification, bounded repair and reverification, review, and completion evidence without creating new execution authority or weakening any existing governance boundary.
principles: Composition delegates to authoritative existing capabilities rather than reimplementing them.

The orchestrator coordinates lifecycle progression but does not itself grant approval, execution authorization, repository mutation authority, commit authority, push authority, deployment authority, credential authority, or network authority.
UNDERSTAND, PLAN, GENERATE, proposal, manifest, artifact, execution-package, execution, verification, repair, review, state, and resume contracts remain authoritative at their existing boundaries.
Requested apply intent is never authorization.
Live model invocation remains separately operator-authorized and credential-gated through the graduated GENERATE-004 boundary.
Generated model content remains candidate source content only and cannot select or broaden governed repository scope.
Execution must continue through the governed execution-package lifecycle; legacy implement apply remains disabled.
Repair remains bounded, failure-code-driven, approved-manifest-driven, reviewed when required, and reverified.
Commit, push, deployment, and other consequential publication actions remain outside automatic objective orchestration.
completionCriteria: A bounded objective can be coordinated through the authoritative graduated front-half and governed downstream lifecycle without duplicating those implementations.
Dry-run lifecycle composition is deterministic and does not mutate repository source files.
Apply intent fails closed unless separately governed execution authorization already exists.
The orchestrator cannot manufacture or reinterpret apply intent as authorization.
Live model invocation remains separately operator-controlled and is not implicitly triggered by objective orchestration.
Generated candidate content cannot broaden specification-approved repository scope.
Execution continues through the existing governed execution-package lifecycle.
Verification, bounded repair, reverification, and review remain authoritative downstream gates.
Objective/session progression records sufficient evidence for safe resume without treating persisted state as authority.
Commit, push, deployment, credential discovery, and automatic publication remain outside the orchestrated lifecycle.
Historical commands and persisted artifacts remain compatible.
